title: Simulating many-engine spacecraft: Exceeding 1 quadrillion degrees of freedom via information geometric regularization
problem: Ultra-high-resolution multi-engine spacecraft CFD simulations require massive computational resources and memory; traditional approaches hit scalability limits.
motivation: Kilometer-scale Earth simulations demand exascale capabilities; advancing CFD techniques enables breakthrough simulations with improved efficiency metrics.
method: Information Geometric Regularization (IGR) with unified memory (CPU-GPU/APU), mixed half/single-precision, and adaptive algorithms on heterogeneous platforms.
key_novelty: First to exceed 1 quadrillion DOF (20x prior record); demonstrates strong scaling to extreme system scales with near-ideal efficiency.
contributions: Record-breaking simulation scale: 200 trillion grid points, 1 quadrillion DOF
80% strong scaling efficiency on full Alps system
Deployment on Frontier, El Capitan, and Alps with ideal weak scaling
limitations: Specific to multi-engine spacecraft domain; IGR may not apply to all CFD problems; energy-to-solution not fully detailed.
